feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital leadership roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid public-sector specialization. It is well written overall, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and opportunities to sharpen impact through clearer outcomes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Strong credibility through concrete scale indicators: 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named platforms/tools.  
- Positioning is focused and coherent: digital platforms, communications systems, governance, and AI-enabled experiences all align well.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across Header, Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Footer/Projects; several themes and tools appear multiple times. Consolidating would improve clarity and save space.  
- Add more outcome-driven results beyond scope metrics: e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, reduced publishing time, campaign performance, adoption rates, or cost savings.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” mixed punctuation in bullets, and spacing around commas (“social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”). “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary filler. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats several competency areas listed elsewhere. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language: “leading” or “delivering” sounds stronger.
- Add one proof point from recent experience, e.g. “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase impact.
- Tighten the second sentence by grouping related capabilities and reducing the long list.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Delivers scalable digital platforms, analytics infrastructure and editorial systems for complex, mission-driven organizations, including a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views and AI-enabled content discovery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Analytics infrastructure,” “editorial systems,” “multimedia production,” and “AI-enabled user experiences” duplicate Core Competencies/Topline Skills.
- Subtitle already signals leadership focus, so the intro can prioritize evidence and scope over another capability list.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be stronger if tightened and made more distinct from adjacent sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, cleaner phrases and keep the list parallel in structure.
- Prioritize the most marketable recent strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, and workflow integration.
- Consider replacing broader items with sharper wording, e.g. “Multi-channel communications operations” → “Cross-channel digital communications.”
- Suggested version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, dashboarding and reporting infrastructure • Cross-channel digital communications • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider using it only if you trim or remove overlapping skills elsewhere.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” is already well established in the header and work experience.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads like a compressed portfolio and overlaps heavily with the recent consulting and NACo experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a concise, parallel bullet.
- Tighten wording: e.g., “AI-powered legislative search” instead of “AI-enabled legislative search experience”; “site-integrated” instead of “connected to the main site.”
- Emphasize scope, audience, or result where possible: campaign growth, policy discovery, member engagement, conference activation, recurring distribution cadence.
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency in formal CV writing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search and We Are Counties Microsite substantially repeat the current freelance role; consider keeping only the most impressive 2–3 projects or adding outcomes not stated above.
- Advocacy Video Series overlaps with multiple NACo roles; avoid repeating responsibilities already covered in Work Experience.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope and relevance, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the project footer and prior NACo entries. Tighten around strategic ownership, technical depth, and outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with impact + client type: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate bullets to 4–5 sharper points, e.g.:
- “Built cross-functional workflows, analytics and governance systems to improve coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Provided hands-on CMS/front-end implementation and troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.”
- “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows and user discovery experience.”
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy, time saved, or engagement gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” and the Drupal microsite work duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and let the footer hold examples.
- “Governance/usability/best practices” overlaps with NACo roles; emphasize what is new or more senior here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management themes already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget.”
- Combine the website bullets and keep the strongest metrics: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-focused; add performance if available: subscriber growth, engagement, open/click rates, follower growth, or campaign results.
- Tighten remaining bullets to emphasize enterprise buildout: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio,” “Implemented analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery,” “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version strategic, not operational.
- Video-programming language overlaps with older NACo roles; emphasize studio buildout and organizational capability here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what changed under your leadership at this level: operating cadence, editorial coordination, and channel growth.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and outcome-based: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper systems point: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and more consistent digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” sound soft; use direct ownership language.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tightened to emphasize higher-level leadership themes not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more distinctive, executive-level phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider swapping “multi-channel communications leadership” to “cross-channel communications leadership” for sharper wording.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is solid but could be stronger as “audience strategy & content planning.”
- If space allows, align terms with recent work by emphasizing “transformation,” “operations,” and “governance” over generic “messaging.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” substantially repeat the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent platform leadership and execution themes rather than repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Remove lower-priority or older items unless central to target roles; keep Drupal first, and consider dropping jQuery to avoid dating the profile.
- If accurate, add scope/level language to match recent experience: “Enterprise Drupal platforms” or “Large-scale website migrations and platform improvement.”
- Keep this section shorter than Technical + IT; let the detailed stack live there.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT” entries for CMS, coding, and automation tools.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies; keep it here only if you trim elsewhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making and optimization outcomes, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as a concise capability line: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • executive/leadership dashboards • SEO, UX and performance optimization”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “executive dashboards” or “decision-support reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- Consider changing “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX and conversion/performance analysis” if accurate; it reads more outcome-oriented.
- Keep only the most differentiating tools/capabilities here; use this section to show strategic analytics leadership, not a full software inventory.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Since GA4/Clarity/Power BI/Looker Studio/BigQuery already appear in recent NACo experience, avoid repeating the exact same list elsewhere.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus multiple work bullets. Make it tighter, more senior, and focused on distinctive capabilities rather than broad production tasks.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: “Broadcast & Event Production” to sound more strategic and concise.
- Replace the list with: “Broadcast video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio buildout and operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems”
- If accurate, add scale/context instead of generic terms, e.g. “broadcast-quality studio operations” or “virtual and hybrid event production for advocacy/member audiences.”
- Drop “editing” unless post-production is a meaningful differentiator; “video production” usually covers it at this level.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” substantially repeat “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies.
- “Studio operations” is already supported by the NACo bullet about building the in-house studio; keep this skills line high-level, not repetitive.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should either add proficiency/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, prioritize by strength/relevance: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Consider adding level/scope only where strongest, e.g., “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; custom microsites)” if your format supports brief qualifiers
- Keep platform names only; avoid repeating broader terms like “CMS modernization” here since they already appear elsewhere

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills > “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, and SharePoint
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor versus your senior enterprise profile unless it supports a notable recent project

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more implementation-focused and emphasize the newer tools most relevant to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; they add little value and date the section.
- Keep jQuery only if still actively used in recent Drupal/front-end work; otherwise remove it to avoid signaling an older stack.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier for impact/context: “front-end implementation, tagging, serverless scripts, deployment automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; consider keeping detail here and shortening the Topline version.
- “Cloudflare Workers” and “GitHub Actions” are strong differentiators—prioritize them over older/general items.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already highlighted elsewhere. Make it more purposeful by grouping tools by function and emphasizing systems you actually built or led recently.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as function-based categories: “Automation & workflow systems: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; Collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most relevant tools first based on recent work; if Airtable/Power Automate/Zapier were central, lead with those and consider dropping one weaker PM tool.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to use: “for editorial planning, approvals, and cross-team coordination.”
- Keep naming consistent with other sections; use “Microsoft Teams” if you spell out Microsoft elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills, so avoid repeating all three tools unless this section is tightened.
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello are somewhat redundant as four similar PM tools; consider listing only 2–3.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this line is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the scale/operational context shown in recent NACo roles. Make it more specific to enterprise email/member engagement rather than a generic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (enterprise email campaigns, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, member communications)**
- If accurate, strengthen further with scope: **…supporting high-volume newsletters and segmented communications to tens of thousands of stakeholders**
- Keep platform names only if all were used meaningfully; otherwise drop the least relevant/oldest tool to tighten the section

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about newsletters reaching tens of thousands; don’t repeat the same outcome here unless adding new context like segmentation or automation
- “Engagement” may also overlap with Core Competencies’ “Multi-channel communications operations”; keep this item tool-focused, not strategic

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” This item should either be tightened to emphasize technical platforms only or differentiated with more implementation-oriented wording.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Analytics Platforms & Experimentation
- Replace with: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI dashboard development
- Swap “SEO” for “Google Search Console” or “performance analysis” to keep this technical/tool-focused rather than mixing in a broader discipline.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie impact to recent work in experience bullets instead of here, e.g., “expanded analytics infrastructure” or “improved leadership reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Nearly duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” (same tools plus SEO/performance analysis).
- “Dashboarding” is vague and overlaps with Looker Studio/Power BI; “KPI dashboard development” is sharper.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Tighten it to emphasize foundational contributions, team-building, and early multimedia/web impact.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to focus on scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make contributions more concrete: add scale if possible for the website refresh, livestreams, or weekly video series (audience size, frequency, event count, turnaround time).
- Clarify leadership without overstating: “mentored” or “provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” is cleaner than “guidance.”
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improve cross-channel publishing workflows, support a major website refresh, and produce recurring livestream and weekly video content while mentoring a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/building the capability, not scaling it.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; frame this as early process development.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and trim broad support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy priorities.”
- Make the second sentence more outcome-oriented: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest/story planning, and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or output: number of episodes, audiences served, cross-team partners, or types of multimedia assets produced.
- Consider a tighter final version: “Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting NACo program and policy priorities. Launched the organization’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production, while supporting digital and multimedia content for program initiatives.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is too broad and repeats stronger digital/media accomplishments in later NACo roles.
- Avoid overemphasizing general communications support here; later positions already show that progression more credibly.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software, workflows, and production capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so tighten it to emphasize tools only.

Suggested edit
- Split tools from capabilities; keep this line software-focused.
- Use parallel phrasing and more specific labels: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator”.
- Replace broad workflow terms with clearer technical capabilities only if they add value, e.g. “Livestream production systems” instead of “Livestream studio workflows”.
- Suggested rewrite: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream production systems • Podcast editing & production”
